text:
Elaine (Design): Quick design check — I'm proposing a 'preview strip' at the top of the alert config that shows which channels will be notified, the effective threshold, and suppression window. Mock: https://figma.redwood/mock-alert-preview. Thoughts on announcing state for screen readers? :microscope:

Matt (Eng): Love the preview strip for quick confirmation. Concern: keyboard focus landing — should it be the first tabbable element or skipped via aria-hidden? :thinking:

Aria (A11y): Don't hide it. Screen readers need that summary. Make it role=\"region\" and aria-label=\"Alert preview\" and ensure focusable via a skip link. Example snippet: `<div role=\"region\" aria-label=\"Alert preview\">`

Elaine (Design): Good call. But visually some teams find it decorative — can we toggle visibility to assistive tech only when there is content? e.g., aria-hidden=\"true\" when empty?

Aditya (Product): Also about badge ordering: current mock sorts by priority then alphabetical. For multi-tenant routing, alphabetical is confusing. Suggest sorting by routing policy, then priority, then name.

Sam (PM): Or show a tiny routing-policy icon before the badge and then alphabetical within each policy. That reduces cognitive load when scanning.

Ben (Docs): Copy nit — 'Suppression window' vs 'Quiet window' vs 'Silence window'. Legal prefers 'suppression', product leans 'quiet'. Recommend standardize on 'suppression window' in the UI and surface 'quiet window' in help text for less-technical folks. :eyes:

Elaine (Design): Agreed. I'll standardize to 'suppression window' in the mock and add an inline helptext that reads: "Suppression window (aka quiet window) — temporarily stop notifications for the selected channels."

Aditya (Product): Accessibility tweak: badge label contrast fails AA in dark mode with current token. Either bump font-weight to 600 or use a slightly lighter badge background. Also ensure the badge removal 'x' is keyboard operable (Enter/Space).

Matt (Eng): +1 on keyboard. Also when the preview shows a fallback channel or model (because of routing/failover), we should surface a small 'why' tooltip on hover and a persistent 'More' button to expose details to screen readers.

design-bot: Deploy preview updated: https://redwood.design/mock/alert-preview-v2 — updated strip + aria fixes. (bot)

Aria (A11y): Quick test with VoiceOver: region is announced but users need a skip-link to jump past it. Suggest a visible but low-contrast "Skip preview" link for keyboard users and ensure `aria-hidden` toggles off only after content loads.

Elaine (Design): Okay — I'll add a skip link and expose a skip target on the main form. I'll update the figma and post a follow-up here. Timeline: EOD updates, demo in standup tomorrow. Anyone want to pair on the screenreader wording?

Ben (Docs): I can pair 10:00am tomorrow to help with wording + helptext examples. :thumbsup:

Sam (PM): One more implementation note: on narrow/mobile, collapse badges into a single pill like "1 channel +2" — make sure collapsed state still has accessible text announcing full channel count and names to screen readers (e.g., `aria-label=\"Channels: pagerduty, slack, email\"`).

Elaine (Design): Noted — will include collapsed-state aria-label in the spec. Thanks all!
